title: Plitvička Jezera Itinerary 2027: 1, 2 and 3 Day Plans
metaDescription: Plan Plitvice Lakes with 1-day and 2-day itineraries, ticket prices from €10 to €40, route lengths, entrances, boat times and local tips for 2027.
content:
## Plitvice Lakes Itinerary at a Glance

Plitvice Lakes National Park (Nacionalni park Plitvička jezera) has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979. It contains 16 named terraced lakes linked by waterfalls and wooden boardwalks. The park is open every day of the year, but hours and available routes change by season. The largest waterfall, Veliki Slap, drops about 78 m and is the standard first-time highlight.

The park has two entrances, a boat on Lake Kozjak and a panoramic shuttle train. Both are included in the ticket price. Swimming is not allowed anywhere in the park.

## Ticket Prices for Plitvice Lakes (2026 Tariff, Check Before 2027)

Prices depend on the season, and in summer on the time of entry.

- **November–March:** adults €10, students €6, children 7–18 €4
- **April, May and October:** adults €23, students €14, children €6
- **June–September:** adults €40, students €25, children €15 before the afternoon cutoff
- **Summer afternoon entry:** €25 adults, €15 students, €9 children (after 16:00 in June–August, after 15:00 in September)
- **Two-day ticket:** adults €15, €39 or €60 depending on season
- **Children under 7:** free

In summer, entry is timed and capped, so buy online for a fixed date and arrival slot. Arrive within your booked window, because late arrivals can be refused. Ticket sales at the gate end mid-afternoon in the off-season, so an arrival after 15:00 in October can mean no entry.

Roughly: a family of two adults and two children aged 7–18 pays €110 in peak summer, but only €68 with afternoon tickets.

## Entrance 1 vs Entrance 2

**Entrance 1 (Ulaz 1)** is at the top of the Lower Lakes, next to Veliki Slap. It is the closest gate to the main viewpoint, and the best place to start if you want to see the waterfall before the crowds arrive.

**Entrance 2 (Ulaz 2)** is the gateway to the Upper Lakes and the boat dock area, and sits close to the park hotels and the main parking lot. It is the more practical start for Route C and the longer routes.

In winter, only Entrance 1 is generally operational, and some boardwalk sections and the boat may be closed because of ice or snow.

## One-Day Itinerary: Route C from Entrance 2

Route C is the best single-day option for most visitors. It covers the Upper and Lower Lakes in 4–6 hours and about 8 km, with the shuttle and boat doing the heavy transport work.

**07:00–08:00:** Arrive at Entrance 2. Parking is paid and fills by 09:30 in July and August.

**08:00–10:00:** Take the shuttle up to the Upper Lakes stop (St. Hill, Station 3) and walk down the boardwalks beside Gornja Jezera. These lakes have more forest and calmer water, and fewer people than the Lower Lakes.

**10:00–12:00:** Continue to the Kozjak boat dock. The electric boat crosses Lake Kozjak, the largest lake in the park, in about 20 minutes.

**12:00–14:00:** Walk the Lower Lakes boardwalks to the base of Veliki Slap. The lower canyon section has the densest boardwalks and the highest crowd levels from 11:00 to 15:00.

**14:00–15:00:** Climb up to Entrance 1 or take the shuttle back to Entrance 2. A short lunch or snack is available at the kiosks near both entrances.

### Short Version: Route A or B (2–3 hours)

Routes A and B suit visitors on a time limit, such as a stop between Zagreb and the coast. Route A is the shortest, at about 3.5 km, and focuses on the Lower Lakes and Veliki Slap. Route B adds a boat ride.

## Two-Day Itinerary

A two-day ticket suits visitors who want a slower pace or a stay near the park.

**Day 1:** Route C, as above, in the morning. Finish by 15:00, then rest.

**Day 2:** Walk Route H or K for the least-visited parts of the park. Start at 07:30 and plan for 6–8 hours on Route K, which is about 18 km. Bring food, since options along the trail are limited.

The two-day ticket costs €60 in peak summer. Two summer afternoon tickets cost €50, but they cover fewer useful hours, because the last boat and shuttle leave early in the evening. For a two-day stay in July or August, the €60 ticket is the better choice.

## Optional Extra Day: Rastoke in Slunj

Rastoke is a small village of watermills and cascades in Slunj, around 35 km north of the park on the road toward Zagreb. Walking the village takes 1–2 hours and costs nothing for the public paths. It is a good lunch stop on a transfer day, with the same type of travertine scenery as Plitvice, but without the entry fee or the crowds.

## Best Time to Visit

- **Late April–May:** high water, strong waterfalls, moderate crowds, €23 entry.
- **September–October:** warm days, autumn colours in October, lower prices from October.
- **June–August:** the most crowded period and the highest price (€40). Go before 09:00 or take the afternoon ticket.
- **Winter:** cheap (€10), but with ice, closed sections and reduced transport. Frozen waterfalls are the main attraction.

The lakes are at their clearest in dry weather. Heavy rain turns parts of the water a cloudy green-brown for a few days.

## How to Get to Plitvice Lakes

- **From Zagreb:** about 135 km, roughly 2 hours by car on the A1 and DC1. Direct buses run to the park, taking about 2–2.5 hours.
- **From Zadar:** about 130 km, roughly 1 hour 45 minutes.
- **From Split:** about 230 km, roughly 3 hours.
- **From Zagreb Airport:** about 150 km, around 2 hours.

Bus stations at both entrances make the park easy to reach without a car. Many travellers use the park as a break on the Zagreb–Split or Zagreb–Zadar route. Left luggage is available near the entrances, which helps on a transit day.

## Where to Stay

Three hotels operate inside the park area: Hotel Jezero, Hotel Plitvice and Hotel Bellevue. They put you within walking distance of Entrance 2, and let you reach the gate at opening time. Outside the park, the villages of Plitvički Ljeskovac, Korenica and Jezerce offer many private apartments and guesthouses, typically cheaper in the shoulder season. Book 2–3 months ahead for July and August.

## Local Tips

- **Start early:** the first two hours after opening are the quietest. By 11:00 in summer, the boardwalks near Veliki Slap are slow-moving.
- **Walk the Upper Lakes first, then go down:** this follows the shuttle and boat flow and keeps most of the walk downhill.
- **Wear shoes with grip:** the wooden boardwalks are slippery when wet.
- **Bring water and snacks:** food options inside the park are limited and priced higher than in nearby villages.
- **Check the last boat and shuttle times** at the first station, particularly in the off-season, when services end earlier.
- **Do not rely on drones, picnics or swimming:** drones are prohibited, and lakeside picnicking and swimming are banned.

The €40 peak-summer ticket is the weakest value of the year. For the same walk in late September or October, the price falls to about €23 at a fraction of the crowd, and a visit then is usually the better choice than a midsummer slot.

## Sample Daily Budget (per adult, 2026 prices)

- Entry: €10–€40
- Parking: paid, per hour or per day, depending on the lot
- Lunch or snack in the park: about €10–€15
- Bus from Zagreb: varies by operator, book in advance in July and August

Guided day trips from Zagreb or Zadar usually start around €75 including entry, and are mostly worth it only for those without a car.

faq.question: How many days do you need at Plitvice Lakes?
faq.answer: One full day is enough for the main Upper and Lower Lakes via Route C (about 8 km, 4–6 hours). A second day suits visitors who want the longer Route K, fewer crowds or a slower pace.

faq.question: How much does a Plitvice Lakes ticket cost?
faq.answer: An adult one-day ticket costs €10 from November to March, €23 in April, May and October, and €40 from June to September. Summer afternoon entry costs €25, and children under 7 enter free.

faq.question: What is the best route at Plitvice Lakes for first-time visitors?
faq.answer: Route C is the best all-round route. It covers the Upper and Lower Lakes, the boat on Lake Kozjak and Veliki Slap in about 4–6 hours.

faq.question: Which entrance should I use, Entrance 1 or Entrance 2?
faq.answer: Use Entrance 1 for the quickest view of Veliki Slap and the Lower Lakes. Use Entrance 2 for Route C and longer routes, because it connects to the Upper Lakes and the boat dock.

faq.question: Can you swim at Plitvice Lakes?
faq.answer: No. Swimming is banned in all lakes of the national park to protect the travertine formations and water quality.

faq.question: Can you visit Plitvice Lakes as a day trip from Zagreb?
faq.answer: Yes. The park is about 135 km and 2 hours from Zagreb by car, with direct buses available. Leave before 07:00 to be at the gate by opening time and finish Route C before the afternoon crowds.

faq.question: Is the boat included in the Plitvice ticket?
faq.answer: Yes. The electric boat on Lake Kozjak and the panoramic shuttle are included in the entrance ticket. In winter the boat may not operate.

quickAnswer: Spend one full day at Plitvice Lakes: enter at 7:00–8:00 via Entrance 2, walk Route C (about 8 km, 4–6 hours) through the Upper and Lower Lakes, and take the free boat and shuttle. Tickets cost €10–€40 depending on season. Add a second day for Rastoke or a quieter route.
